report:
No significant knee effusion. There is horizontal tearing through the posteromedial corner of the medial meniscus. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  The tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage is normal. Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues.  
Conclusion: Undisplaced tearing of the posteromedial corner of the medial meniscus.

No significant knee effusion. A small free edge radial tear is noted along the posterior body of the medial meniscus. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  The tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage is normal. Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues.  
Conclusion: Tiny free edge radial tear of the posterior body of the medial meniscus.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Arthritis.
Comparison: [REDACTED]. [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Tricompartmental osteophytes.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Oblique undersurface tear of the body/posterior horn. No significant peripheral extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Areas of full-thickness cartilage loss along the inner aspect of the weightbearing femoral condyle and peripheral/posterior tibial plateau.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Complex tearing of the posterior horn, body and anterior horn with a complete radial tear of the anterior root. Moderate peripheral extrusion of the body segment with underlying reactive marrow edema at the anterolateral aspect of the tibial plateau.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Areas of full-thickness cartilage loss along the weightbearing femoral condyle and tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Areas of high-grade cartilage loss with full thickness fissuring along the medial trochlea and patellar median ridge/lateral facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Intact, with some degenerative signal.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Chronic partial tearing.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 7 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Prominent subcutaneous veins, possibly varicosities. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Tricompartmental osteoarthritis, severe in the lateral compartment.
2.	Complex tearing of the lateral meniscus.
3.	Oblique undersurface tear of the medial meniscal posterior horn.

Findings:  No significant joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No sinister bone marrow changes. 6 mm hypointense focus in the lateral aspect of the medial femoral condyle. No surrounding bone marrow edema. Findings likely represent an incidental enostosis.  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments. Intact menisci.  Normal appearance of the pes anserine tendons, distal biceps femoris tendon, distal iliotibial band and popliteus tendon.  Intact extensor mechanism. No evidence of fat pad impingement.  Low-grade chondral thinning along the anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. Otherwise relatively well-maintained tricompartmental hyaline articular cartilage.  
Conclusion:  Low-grade chondral thinning along the anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle.
